title: Payment Gateway Charges in India: Are Free Payment Gateways Really Free?
summary: Understand payment gateway charges in India, including transaction fees, hidden costs, GST, settlement charges, and why “free” payment gateways may not be completely free.
body_markdown:
Table of Contents


Toggle


Every payment gateway in India charges something to process a payment. What has changed is how that cost is structured, and how long a new business can avoid it.


Right now, Cashfree runs a festive offer for new merchants: 0% platform fee on eligible domestic transactions, up to a total of ₹20 lakh in GMV. It applies to businesses that signed up on or after 21st July 2026, and it runs till 31st March 2027.


Below, you’ll find every charge that goes into a payment gateway, what “free” actually covers, how GST changes your real cost, and how Cashfree compares with other payment gateways.


##


Is There Really a Free Payment Gateway?


For years, “free payment gateway” was a marketing line with little behind it. Every gateway had a setup fee, a maintenance charge or a transaction cut somewhere. Processing a payment still costs money somewhere in the chain. That part hasn’t changed.


What has changed is who absorbs that cost, and for how long. Cashfree’s festive offer waives the platform fee on eligible domestic payments through UPI, debit and credit cards, net banking and wallets. It lasts until you cross ₹20 lakh in total GMV or the offer ends on 31st March 2027, whichever comes first.


So is it free? Within limits, yes. Three things still apply.


**GST is not waived** : Cashfree still deducts 18% GST, calculated on the standard 1.95% fee, even when the platform fee is zero.


**Some payment methods sit outside the offer** : American Express, Diners Club, corporate cards, prepaid cards, EMI, Pay Later, e-mandates and international payments are charged at standard rates.


**The cap is cumulative, not monthly:** Once you process ₹20 lakh in total, standard pricing kicks in automatically.


Read past the headline number before you build a business model on any “free” claim. Cashfree’s included.


##


Elements in Payment Gateway Charges


Payment gateway charges constitute of multiple charges from fees for setup to TDR and so on. Let’s understand the common payment gateway charges individually.


### 1. **Setup Fee**


This is a one-time fee paid when you integrate a payment gateway on your website/application. The fee is non-recurring in nature. This fee is to cover expenses on


- Onboarding a merchant (eg. document verification, KYC of business, physical verification) and
- Infrastructure cost ( eg every time a bank net banking option is enabled, the payment gateway service provider needs to share merchant details with respective bank and then bank activates the account with it, for this bank may charge some fees)


Cashfree charges zero setup fee. There’s no upfront cost to get started, regardless of your transaction volume.


### 2. **Annual/Monthly Maintenance Fees (AMC)**


You might be required to pay a pre-determined sum of money or fee every month/yearly to the payment gateway provider as maintenance charges. These are charges to cover operating expenses, software maintenance, and technology upgradation cost).


The annual/monthly maintenance cost differs based on the following factors


- Mode of payments activated
- Types of integration ( for eg if you have web checkout, the maintenance charges will be lower, while the charges can be high if you opt for advanced integrations like seamless integration)
- Payment gateway features you opt (for eg integrated refund management, auto-billing service etc may be additional features)


Cashfree charges zero AMC on its standard plan. You only pay the platform fee on transactions you actually process, whether that’s 0% under the festive offer or the standard rate afterward. An AMC applies only if you choose Cashfree’s optional premium services, such as a dedicated account manager with fortnightly check-ins and priority support with a 30-minute response time.


### **3. Transaction discount rate ( TDR )**


TDR, also called platform fee or[MDR](https://www.cashfree.com/blog/merchant-discount-rate-mdr/) , is the percentage charged on each successful transaction. It changes with the payment mode. UPI sits at the low end. EMI, Pay Later and international cards cost more.


Here’s what Cashfree currently charges:

##


**Cashfree Festive Offer: Who Qualifies and What’s Excluded**


The 0% offer is generous, but it has rules. Know them before you plan your cash flow around it.


**Who qualifies:** New merchants who signed up on or after 21st July 2026 and completed KYC and account activation during the offer period. The offer applies automatically. No promo code, no request.


**Who doesn’t:** Merchants who were already transacting on Cashfree before 21st July 2026. Merchants referred through partners or resellers. Accounts on custom pricing. A few business categories, including schools and local commuter transport.


**One offer per business:** It can be used once per PAN or bank account. If you open multiple merchant IDs under the same PAN, only the first activated one qualifies.


**The credit card check:** Once your total GMV reaches ₹1 lakh, Cashfree looks at your payment mix. If credit cards make up 60% or more of your volume, the offer can be withdrawn. Most UPI-heavy businesses never get close to this. High-ticket businesses, where customers mostly pay by card, should check their mix first.


**When it ends:** Whichever comes first: you use up the ₹20 lakh, the campaign ends on 31st March 2027, or you’re disqualified for misuse. Unused value lapses. It can’t be carried forward or exchanged for cash.


**What you get alongside it:** T+1 settlement by 8 PM as the default cycle, plus a dedicated account manager if your business is GST-registered.


##


**How GST Changes Your Real Cost**


A 1.95% fee is never just 1.95%. GST at 18% sits on top of every platform fee. Here’s what that looks like on a ₹1,00,000 card payment.


**Line Item** **Standard Pricing (1.95%)** **During Festive Offer (0%)**


Sale value ₹1,00,000 ₹1,00,000


Platform fee ₹1,950 ₹0


GST at 18% ₹351 ₹351 (calculated on 1.95%)


Total deducted ₹2,301 ₹351


Amount you receive ₹97,699 ₹99,649


Effective cost 2.30% 0.35%


Notice the GST line. Even during the offer, Cashfree deducts GST worked out on the standard 1.95% rate. So your effective cost on eligible payments is about 0.35%, not zero. Still a fraction of the usual 2.30%.


Running a GST-registered business? You can usually claim[input tax credit](https://www.cashfree.com/blog/input-tax-credit-gst/) on this GST, which brings your net cost down further. Your CA can confirm how it applies to you.


##


**UPI Charges From 15th October 2026: What Changes for Merchants**


Since January 2020, UPI merchant payments carried zero MDR by law. That changes on 15th October 2026, when NPCI’s new framework kicks in for specific higher-value payments.


**UPI Payment Type** **Merchant Charge from 15th October 2026**


Merchant payments up to ₹2,000 No MDR


Bank-account-funded merchant payments above ₹2,000 0.4%, capped at ₹300 per transaction


Railways, telecom, insurance and fuel payments above ₹2,000 Flat ₹5 per transaction


Small merchants under the P2PM framework No MDR


UPI AutoPay mandates Outside the new framework


Person-to-person transfers No charge


What does that mean in rupees? A ₹5,000 UPI payment carries ₹20 in MDR. A ₹1,00,000 payment would work out to ₹400, but the cap brings it down to ₹300.


Your customers don’t pay any of this. It’s a merchant-side charge, and you shouldn’t add a UPI surcharge at checkout.


For the full rules, read our guide on UPI Charges Above ₹2,000:[New MDR Rules, Rates and Merchant Impact](https://www.cashfree.com/blog/upi-charges-new-mdr-rules/) . To see how the new rate applies on your Cashfree account, check the pricing page or ask your account manager.


### **Does the Payment Gateway Service Provider Get the Whole TDR?**


No, these fee amounts are split between multiple parties to the transaction. Typically, here’s how a 2% charge might be split


- 1.25%: The issuing bank (the card holder’s bank) – applies only for card payments
- 0.15%: Card networks like Visa, Mastercard, Rupay (NPCI) and other intermediaries
- 0.25%: The acquiring bank ( the payment gateway’s bank)
- 0.10%: Payment switch provider – technology service provider for an acquiring bank to connect to card networks and process transactions
- 0.25%: Your merchant account provider (payment gateway service provider who onboards you.

Most payment gateways in India now quote similar headline rates. The real differences show up in fixed fees, offer size, settlement speed and what’s bundled in. Here’s how Cashfree compares.

Typical ranges are based on publicly listed pricing from major Indian payment gateways as of October 2026. All figures exclude GST.


**What the bigger cap means in rupees.** Take a new business processing ₹10 lakh a month in eligible domestic payments. Here’s the platform fee over its first three months (₹30 lakh in total).


**First 3 Months** **Cashfree (₹20 Lakh Offer, then 1.95%)** **Typical Offer (₹5 Lakh or 90 Days, then 2%)**


Volume at 0% platform fee ₹20,00,000 ₹5,00,000


Volume charged at standard rate ₹10,00,000 ₹25,00,000


Platform fee paid ₹19,500 ₹50,000


That’s ₹30,500 more in your account over three months, before GST. The gap grows if your business ramps up faster.


A few things to check before you pick any offer:


**Your payment mix.** Excluded methods like EMI, Amex and international cards are charged at standard rates everywhere.


**Credit card share.** Some offers, Cashfree’s included, can be withdrawn if credit cards dominate your sales.


**The rate after the offer.** It applies to every rupee you process for years after the promotion ends.


**Settlement speed.** Faster default settlement means less working capital tied up.


##


Cashfree Payment Gateway: What You Actually Pay


New merchants who signed up on or after 21st July 2026 pay 0% platform fee on eligible domestic payments. That lasts until they cross ₹20 lakh in total GMV or reach 31st March 2027, whichever comes first. GST is still charged on the standard 1.95% rate.


After that, eligible domestic payments cost 1.95% plus GST. No setup fee. No AMC on the standard plan.


That ₹20 lakh window is four times the size of the typical ₹5 lakh offer elsewhere, and it runs through the rest of FY27 instead of just 90 days. For a business heading into the festive and year-end rush, that’s money you can put into ads, inventory or logistics instead of gateway fees.


**You also get:**


**Next-day settlement:** T+1 by 8 PM as the default cycle during the offer.


**A dedicated account manager:** For GST-registered businesses.


**Free add-on products:** Payment Links, Payment Forms and softPOS at no extra cost with your gateway account.

##


**Frequently Asked Questions**


#### **Is Cashfree’s payment gateway really free?**


For new merchants, mostly yes, within limits. If you signed up on or after 21st July 2026, you pay 0% platform fee on eligible domestic payments (UPI, cards, net banking and wallets) up to ₹20 lakh in total GMV, till 31st March 2027. GST is still charged, and methods like EMI, Pay Later, Amex, prepaid cards and international cards are excluded.


#### **How much does the Cashfree payment gateway cost after the offer ends or the cap is crossed?**


Eligible domestic payments move to the standard 1.95% plus GST. There’s no setup fee and no AMC on the standard plan either way.


#### **Does Cashfree charge anything for UPI payments?**


UPI is charged as per applicable law. From 15th October 2026, a 0.4% MDR, capped at ₹300, applies to specified bank-account-funded UPI merchant payments above ₹2,000. Payments up to ₹2,000 stay free, and your customers never pay this charge.


#### **Is there an annual maintenance charge (AMC) on Cashfree?**


Not on the standard plan. Cashfree charges zero AMC and zero setup fee. An AMC applies only if you opt for premium services like a dedicated account manager with fortnightly check-ins and 30-minute priority support.


#### **How does Cashfree’s zero-fee offer compare to other payment gateways?**


Cashfree’s offer covers ₹20 lakh in total GMV and runs till 31st March 2027. Many other 0% offers stop at ₹5 lakh or 90 days. Also compare excluded payment methods, credit card conditions and the rate you’ll pay once the offer ends.


#### **Is GST charged during Cashfree’s 0% offer?**


Yes. Cashfree deducts 18% GST calculated on the standard 1.95% rate, even when the platform fee is waived. On a ₹1,00,000 payment, that’s ₹351.


#### **Can existing Cashfree merchants get the festive offer?**


No. Merchants who transacted on Cashfree before 21st July 2026 aren’t eligible. The offer is also limited to one merchant ID per PAN or bank account.


#### **What happens if most of my sales come from credit cards?**


Once your GMV reaches ₹1 lakh, Cashfree checks your payment mix. If credit cards make up 60% or more of it, the offer can be withdrawn and standard rates will apply from then on.


#### **What are Cashfree payout charges?**


Payouts cost ₹3 to ₹15 per transfer, depending on the amount and whether you use NEFT, RTGS or IMPS/UPI. GST and bank charges are extra.


#### **What does instant settlement cost on Cashfree?**


Instant settlement carries a 0.30% platform fee, excluding GST. The final rate can vary with the settlement type you choose and your business risk profile.
